title: Merge Intervals

statement.hi: Ek array `intervals` diya hai jahan `intervals[i] = [start, end]`. Saare **overlapping** intervals ko merge karo aur bache hue non-overlapping intervals return karo jo saare input ko cover karein. Result ko **start ke badhte order** me return karo. (`[1,4]` aur `[4,5]` overlap maane jaate hain.)
statement.en: Given an array `intervals` where `intervals[i] = [start, end]`, merge all **overlapping** intervals and return the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the input. Return the result **sorted by start**. (`[1,4]` and `[4,5]` count as overlapping.)

hi: Pehle intervals ko start ke hisaab se sort karo.
Sorted order me, naya interval sirf last merged interval se hi overlap kar sakta hai.
en: Sort the intervals by start first.
In sorted order, a new interval can only overlap the last merged interval.

explain.hi: [1,3] aur [2,6] overlap karte hain, isliye [1,6] ban jaata hai.
explain.en: [1,3] and [2,6] overlap, so they merge into [1,6].

explain.hi: [1,4] aur [4,5] touch karte hain, isliye overlap maane jaate hain.
explain.en: [1,4] and [4,5] touch, so they count as overlapping.

approach.hi: Intervals ko start se sort karo. Phir ek-ek karke dekho: agar current ka start last merged ke end se ≤ hai to end ko max se badha do, warna naya interval push karo. Sort ki wajah se O(n log n) time, O(n) output space.
approach.en: Sort the intervals by start. Walk through them: if the current start is ≤ the end of the last merged interval, extend that end with max; otherwise push a new interval. O(n log n) time for the sort, O(n) output space.
